solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spot a piece that's unusual in bishop's office

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman notices that an odd item has turned up in the bishop's study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges SPOT A PIECE; 'that's' and 'in' are link words. 'Office' here means a post or position, not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The episcopate is the rank, term or position held by a bishop.

clue.text: See with unusual perception the end of history

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is perception beyond the normal senses

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, taken from history

explanation.surface: A psychic claims second sight lets them view how history finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a literary synonym for see.

clue.text: Where proverbial annoying mobile user is well organised!

definitions.text: Where proverbial annoying mobile user is
definitions.meaning: the stock irritating phone caller announces loudly that they are on a railway carriage
a phrase meaning in proper order, all arranged and under way

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both aboard a railway carriage and, idiomatically, in good order and progressing.

clue.text: A c-cougher can't get loose — it means coughing up is postponed!

definitions.text: it means coughing up is postponed

indicators.note: letters that get loose break free of their order and can be reassembled

explanation.surface: A stammering cougher cannot shake free of a fit, with a pun on coughing up money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get loose' rearranges A C-COUGHER CAN'T. 'Coughing up' is slang for paying, so the definition describes buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A store credit arrangement lets a customer buy goods now and pay the bill later.

clue.text: Chum having fun has quiet wager before end of game

indicators.note: in this down clue the earlier pieces come above the following one

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, played quietly
to lay a bet is to wager
checkmate, shortened to mate, ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: A friend out for fun places a modest bet just before the match finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a companion one plays with, a friend in fun.

clue.text: Shot finally getting to a flagpole

definitions.text: Shot finally getting to a flagpole

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Shot

parts.note: in golf the pin is the flagstick marking the hole

explanation.surface: A golfer's stroke at last reaches the flag on the green.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: a short putt that finally reaches the hole, where the PIN is the golf flagstick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap-in is a very short golf putt knocked into the hole beside the flag.

clue.text: Sour-tempered person that may be seen at the seaside

definitions.text: that may be seen at the seaside
definitions.meaning: a shore creature found in rock pools on the beach

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a grouch (as in crabby) and also the clawed crustacean found on beaches.

clue.text: Breathe with hesitation mounting tall part of building

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a church steeple pauses, panting, as they go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns ER upwards to RE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To respire is the formal word for to breathe.

clue.text: Brasenose's fantastic women — noble types

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful, so the letters are jumbled freely

explanation.surface: Female students at Brasenose, an Oxford college, are praised as wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges all ten letters of BRASENOSE'S, the final S included. Brasenose is a college of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronesses are female peers, or wives of barons, so women of noble rank.

clue.text: A new plumbing device seen around Indian city

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a tap is the valve on a pipe or sink

explanation.surface: An up-to-date bathroom fitting has been spotted somewhere in an Indian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' turns the whole of A, N and TAP backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: Patna is the capital of the state of Bihar in India.

clue.text: Domestic animal is eaten by jungle beast by river — prime bit of food?

indicators.note: being eaten puts these words within the beast that swallows them

parts.note: an ape lives in the jungle
a pet is an animal kept in the home
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A household pet is devoured by an ape near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by' signals the container; the second 'by' is only a link. 'Prime' plays on priming the appetite, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser is a small dish served first to stimulate the appetite for the meal.

clue.text: In play watch a done-for Macbeth

indicators.note: words in play are moving about freely and can be rearranged

explanation.surface: In Shakespeare's tragedy, watch as Macbeth is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In play' rearranges WATCH A DONE-FOR, and also nods to the play Macbeth, in which the witches hail Macbeth by this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is named this Scottish title early in Shakespeare's play before becoming king.

clue.text: Logical reasoning required to shift great mountain

indicators.note: to shift is to move things about, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Moving a huge mountain calls for some clear thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' rearranges GREAT MOUNTAIN; 'required to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Argumentation is the process of reasoning methodically to reach a conclusion.

clue.text: Star sapper in battle? Engineers can make use of such

definitions.text: Engineers can make use of such

indicators.note: things in battle are thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A heroic army engineer at war; the Royal Engineers find such kit useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in battle' rearranges STAR SAPPER. A sapper is a military engineer, which supports the surface but is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Replacement components are what mechanics and engineers fit when repairing machines.

clue.text: Ornamental items, underwear? Aim to be seen in such!

indicators.note: the aim is seen inside the underwear, placed within it

parts.note: pants are underpants, a type of underwear
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A cheeky look at jewellery: underwear, and a goal of being spotted wearing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' just points back to the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendants are jewels that hang from a chain worn around the neck.

clue.text: Aboard ship there's still a cut-down version of ball game

indicators.note: placed aboard the ship means set between its two letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
even can mean still, as in even better

explanation.surface: Even on board a vessel, a shortened form of the sport is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' as EVEN is the sense of 'even/still more'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is a seven-a-side form of rugby, quicker and smaller than the full game.

clue.text: Duck sitting on bank maybe concealing a shrub

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

indicators.note: the lender hides the letter inside itself

parts.note: a bank is an example of a lender of money

explanation.surface: A water bird perched on a riverbank hides among the bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' tempts as the riverbank but is a money lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an evergreen flowering shrub of the Mediterranean, poisonous in all its parts.

clue.text: Revolutionary university and established church bound together by contract

parts.note: red is a byword for a revolutionary communist
CE stands for the Church of England, the established church in England

explanation.surface: A radical college and the state church are tied by a binding agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun for a legal agreement, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to shrink or make smaller.

clue.text: Figure formed by various characters in dance full of energy

indicators.note: the scrambled word holds the next piece inside it
the characters, or letters, of the word come in a varied order

parts.note: go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: Dancers in assorted costumes form a shape on a lively dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various characters in' makes DECAN, which 'full of' then wraps around the energy piece. 'Figure' is a shape, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a geometric figure with ten sides.

clue.text: Former sweetheart's love starts to look decidedly feeble and weak

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O

indicators.note: the starts to words are their opening letters

parts.note: a lame excuse is a weak one

explanation.surface: An ex-partner's affection begins to seem very poor and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a past lover, someone once romantically involved with you.

clue.text: Exams? Everything's crammed in the night before!

indicators.note: something crammed in is pushed inside the other piece

parts.note: everything is all, and the 's adds S
an eve is the evening before an event

explanation.surface: A student revises everything at the last minute before the exams.
explanation.walkthrough: A LEVELS are the British school-leaving exams taken at about 18. 'Crammed' looks like last-minute study but means put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A levels are the advanced-level examinations taken in British schools, usually at 18.

clue.text: Envisage accompanying chum to fantastic cinema

parts.note: to picture something is to envisage it
a pal is a chum or friend
ace is slang for excellent or fantastic

explanation.surface: Imagine going along with a friend to a wonderful film show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanying' and 'to' just link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture palace is an old-fashioned name for a cinema, from the grand early movie theatres.

clue.text: Cheer from employee finally out of office

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of employee

parts.note: late can mean former, no longer holding a post, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A worker is happy to be away from the office at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of office' looks like an email auto-reply but means no longer in post.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to cheer them, filling them with joy.

clue.text: Gap in wood almost making one cheerful

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a glade is an open space in a forest

explanation.surface: A clearing in the forest that lifts one's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad is a synonym for happy or pleased.

clue.text: Description of reliable man not left wanting round of applause

parts.note: right is the opposite of left
give a big hand means a round of applause

explanation.surface: A dependable fellow, not abandoned, still waits for some clapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left wanting' looks like one phrase but 'not left' is one piece and 'wanting' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is someone's most trusted and dependable assistant.

clue.text: Live as wife in a sort of depression

indicators.note: the wife's letter goes inside the hollow

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded hollow in the ground
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogy

explanation.surface: A spouse lives on in a state of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood; here it is a hollow in land.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or live in a place.

clue.text: Furore — no time to go down passively

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is taken away

parts.note: to make a stink is to cause a furore or row

explanation.surface: An uproar dies down, with no time left to fight it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that sinks goes under without resisting, simply descending.

clue.text: Mistake is admitted by old rocker threatened with violence

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so these go inside the rocker

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British rock and roll youth
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: An ageing rock fan confesses to a mistake after being menaced.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is short for Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth cult of rock and roll fans.
explanation.definitionFit: To be terrorised is to be intimidated by threats or acts of violence.
